paragraph: Single-family is the core of Little Ferry with 16 sales over six months at a median of $622,000, mostly three and four-bedroom colonials and bi-levels with a few capes, two baths being typical. A little over half sold above asking and the median days on market was 34, so this is competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes are moving, and you should expect competition on the good ones without assuming every listing turns into a bidding war. Condos and townhouses are the second real tier, 13 sales at a median of $294,500, most of them one-bedroom, one-bath units. That tier is the tightest of the three: a median of 19 days on market and a sale-to-list ratio slightly above list. Two-families are a thin slice at three sales with a median of $611,000, and the 169-day median days on market there tells you those sellers waited for the right buyer rather than pricing to move fast. Monthly counts are too small to read a trend from, so anchor on the six-month numbers. If you're weighing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and yard of a single-family, the low-maintenance of a condo, or the rental income of a two-family.
